result.title: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS Manager of Managers Search
result.summary: The Cook County Retirement Board is seeking proposals (RFP No. 25-0004) from qualified firms providing institutional manager-of-managers services across domestic equity, international equity, and fixed income. Proposal documents are available only from the Fund or its consultant, Callan LLC; unauthorized reproduction or use of documents from other sources is prohibited. The quiet period runs from Board authorization of the RFP until selection or completion of the process. Responders must not contact Board members, Fund staff, or the Fund about the RFP; all written inquiries and communications must go to the designated contact. The restrictions promote equal access to information, accurate communication, and a fair, efficient search. Offering anything of value to Board members or Fund staff is prohibited, and violations may disqualify a responder.

result.title: SECTION 2: OVERVIEW
result.summary: The section describes the Cook County public defined benefit Fund, established in 1926 under the Illinois Pension Code, its benefits and approximately $14.7 billion in assets and allocation targets as of September 2025. It seeks one manager-of-managers for up to $350 million to build domestic equity, international equity, and fixed income portfolios, targeting benchmark outperformance over 5–10 years. Services include market research and sub-manager screening; documented investment, operational, legal, and background due diligence; IPS-aligned portfolio construction; ongoing manager, risk, compliance, valuation, fee, and performance monitoring; transparent holdings and monthly/quarterly reporting; and coordination with Fund staff, Board, and committees. Responders must meet SEC or equivalent registration, track-record preference, under-$30-billion firm AUM, capitalization, stability, and audited-financial-statement requirements; smaller underlying managers are preferred. They must avoid contingent-fee solicitation, comply with Fund policy and Illinois law, affirm fiduciary status, and disclose fees, ownership, officers, and subcontractors. Engagement requires a binding agreement, fiduciary acknowledgment, side-letter acceptance or revisions, and satisfactory insurance from A- or better-rated insurers.

nodes.title: Fund Overview and Manager-of-Managers Objectives
key_items: 2.2 LONG-TERM PORTFOLIO OBJECTIVES FOR THE ASSIGNMENT
nodes.summary: Established in 1926, the Fund is a public defined benefit plan governed by the Illinois Pension Code, providing retirement, death, and disability benefits to Cook County employees and eligible survivors and dependents. As of September 30, 2025, it held approximately $14.7 billion in assets, with targets of 32% domestic equity, 20% international equity, 26% fixed income, 9% real estate, 5% private equity, 3% hedge funds, 2% private infrastructure, 2% private credit, and 1% cash. The Fund seeks one qualified manager of managers for up to $350 million, experienced in identifying and vetting underlying managers. The mandate will build and manage domestic equity, international equity, and fixed income portfolios, aiming to outperform each asset-class benchmark and the program’s custom benchmark over typical measurement periods of 5–10 years.

nodes.title: 2.3 SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED
key_items: 2.3.1 Analyze and Screen the Underlying Manager Firms
2.3.3 Portfolio Construction; 2.3.4 Monitor the Portfolio of Underlying Managers; 2.3.5 Reporting
2.3.4 Monitor the Portfolio of Underlying Managers
nodes.summary: Provide manager-based investment services across domestic equity, international equity, and fixed income in coordination with investment staff. Periodically analyze markets and screen sub-managers for team quality, suitable strategies, and strong risk-adjusted performance. Conduct and document due diligence covering investment drivers and risks, performance verification and peer comparisons, return repeatability, operational/business risks, legal terms and agreements, interviews, background checks, references, and investment memoranda. Construct portfolios consistent with the CCPF Investment Policy Statement (IPS), guidelines, benchmarks, and objectives. Continuously monitor managers’ activities, operations, agreement compliance, valuation, fees, and expense/profit allocation; identify issues such as style drift, limits, risk levels, and key-person events; maintain oversight procedures and resolve discrepancies. Report material developments, provide holdings transparency, monthly accounting/performance reconciliations, and monthly and quarterly fund- and manager-level reports. Coordinate with Fund Management on lineup changes, IPS graduation provisions, manager graduation recommendations, requested analyses, Board or committee meetings, and requested education and research materials.

nodes.title: 2.4 MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ASSIGNMENT
nodes.summary:
2.4 MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ASSIGNMENT
The Responder must be registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) pursuant to the Investment Advisors Act of 1940 or a bank or insurance company similarly registered.
The Responder should preferably have a three-year performance track record implementing the relevant strategy on behalf of institutional investors. This track record may include the candidate strategy, or experience implementing the strategy at a former entity or firm.
The Responder must have less than $30 Billion in assets under management at the firm level.
It is preferred that the Responder selects underlying managers with no more than $10 Billion in assets under management.
The Responder must be well capitalized and stable. The Responder’s financial statements (audited) must be made available during the course of review for this RFP.

nodes.title: 2.5 GENERAL QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ASSIGNMENT
nodes.summary: Responders may not use contingent-fee third-party marketing agents or pay direct or indirect solicitation or placement fees related to the Fund account. They must review and comply with the Fund’s Investment Policy, execute an affirmation acknowledging fiduciary status under Illinois law, be familiar with and comply with Articles 1 and 9 of the Illinois Pension Code, and meet its disclosure requirements, including Sections 1-113.14(c)(5) and 1-113.21. Disclosures must explain fee calculation and measurement, including direct and indirect fees, commissions, penalties, compensation, and expense reimbursements; identify the Responder, related parent, controlling-interest, subsidiary entities, and owners with over 7.5% ownership or distributive income share, and executive officers; and list subcontractors, their addresses, and expected payments. Subcontractor disclosure excludes non-investment-related professionals and services.

nodes.title: 2.6 SPECIFICATIONS FOR THE ASSIGNMENT
nodes.summary: At engagement, the Fund and selected firm(s) will agree to a binding final agreement covering services, investment guidelines, and performance expectations; it will supersede the RFP. The firm(s) must acknowledge in writing their fiduciary duty under Illinois law to the Fund and in managing its manager-of-managers portfolio. They must confirm willingness to sign the proposed side letter (Attachment D) or suggest revisions, and maintain insurance throughout the relationship at coverage levels satisfactory to the Fund, from insurers rated A- or better by A.M. Best & Company.

result.title: SECTION 3: TIMELINE AND INSTRUCTIONS FOR SUBMISSION
result.summary: The RFP schedule runs from issuance on December 4, 2025, through written questions due December 12, Q&A posting December 19, submissions January 9, staff presentations February 9, and finalist presentations to the Investment Committee February 26, 2026; dates may change, with updates posted online. Questions must be emailed to cookcountyRFP@countypension.com and ccpfMOM@callan.com by noon CDT December 12. Afterward, unclear questions should be answered based on the responder’s interpretation; written communications prevail. Proposals are due by 4:30 p.m. CDT January 9; there is no set award date, and staff may interview firms in February. Responders must update Callan’s online database and complete Attachment E. The Fund may request information or clarifications and permit corrections. Email zipped submissions to the designated contacts. Include a signed cover letter, signed Affirmation Statement (Attachment B, Appendix A), completed Attachments C and E, and a complete proposal PDF. Proposals must clearly answer all questions; incomplete proposals are disqualified and late proposals rejected.

result.title: SECTION 4: DISCLOSURE
result.summary: The Fund may reject proposals, seek clarification or additional information, retain submitted proposals, modify or end the engagement, amend the RFP or agreement, and use ideas from any proposal. Proposals become Fund property and may be publicly disclosed under Illinois FOIA. Responders seeking protection must specifically mark and separate exempt material; blanket designations are not honored, the Fund decides what may be disclosed, and it may require written justification. Responders may need to defend their designation and indemnify the Fund for claims arising from either nondisclosure or legally required disclosure. The Fund pays no proposal-preparation costs and may waive or allow correction of nonmaterial variances at its discretion. Responders must follow Fund ethics policies and gift restrictions; a selected firm must affirm the Investment Policy and fiduciary duty or risk disqualification. Illinois law and courts govern. Submission accepts RFP conditions unless clearly noted and confirmed in the final agreement.

result.title: SECTION 5: SELECTION PROCESS
key_items: 5.1 EVALUATION OF PROPOSALS AND CANDIDATE QUALIFICATION
result.summary: The Fund seeks a manager of managers with competitive performance, a clear investment philosophy and risk controls, a stable and experienced team, institutional and tax-exempt clients, strong service and collaboration, proactive communication, transparency and governance, and competitive fees. Fund Staff and Callan evaluate proposals against RFP criteria and supporting materials; firms may be invited to present to the Investment Committee or Board, with selection requiring Board approval. The Fund may award to the best-fit firm, reject noncompliant proposals, or defer or make no hire. Qualified emerging managers meeting Board search and RFP qualification criteria must be invited for final consideration; where several qualify, Staff may select the strongest candidates to present. The term “Emerging Investment Manager” follows 40 ILCS 5/1-109.1(4). After the process, the Board’s decision becomes public, including selected firms, mandate amounts, fee-determination basis, and Board-approved selection factors.
